records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֤י בְנֵֽי־לָבָן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָקַ֣ח יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֵ֖ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֑ינוּ וּמֵאֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔ינוּ עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַכָּבֹ֖ד הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he heard [the] words of [the] sons of Laban, saying, has taken Jacob all that [belonged] to our father, and from what [belonged] to our father he has made all this wealth.
pieces: Jacob heard what Laban's sons were saying: "Jacob has taken everything that belonged to our father. All his riches come from our father's property."

L.1: And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, "Jacob has taken all that was our father's, and from what was our father's he has gained all this wealth."

R.1: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining about him. They said, "Jacob has taken all our father's property. He became rich by taking what was our father's."

decisions.choice: wealth (kavod): literally "weight"
decisions.reason: The word kavod means weight, and so wealth or honor; it is the usual word for "glory". Here it is the weight of Jacob's possessions.

decisions.choice: Jacob has taken all: the sons' charge
decisions.reason: The charge is exaggerated: Laban still has flocks (verse 19). But Jacob's wealth did come from Laban's herds (30:37-43), and the sons see their inheritance shrinking.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jacob at the start of a new chapter.

records.source: וַיַּ֥רְא יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י לָבָ֑ן וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵינֶ֛נּוּ עִמּ֖וֹ כִּתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃
records.gloss: And saw Jacob [the] face of Laban, and behold, it [was] not with him as yesterday [and] three days ago.
pieces: Jacob also saw from Laban's face that he no longer felt as he once had toward him.

L.2: And Jacob saw the face of Laban, and look, it was not toward him as before.

R.2: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly to him as he had been before.

decisions.choice: as before: literally "as yesterday and the day before"
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as in the past" (Exodus 5:7). Laban's attitude, seen in his face, has changed.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֔ב שׁ֛וּב אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ אֲבוֹתֶ֖יךָ וּלְמוֹלַדְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאֶֽהְיֶ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH to Jacob, return to [the] land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Jacob, "Return to your fathers' land and to your own people. I will be with you."

L.3: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Jacob, "Return to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you."

R.3: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Jacob, "Go back to the land where your father and grandfather lived, to your own family. I will be with you."

decisions.choice: I will be with you: the promise of Bethel
decisions.reason: God promised at Bethel to be with Jacob and to bring him back to this land (28:15). Now the time has come, and Jacob tells his wives of the command (verse 13).

decisions.choice: where your father and grandfather lived
decisions.reason: Readable says who "your fathers" are: Abraham and Isaac.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיִּקְרָ֖א לְרָחֵ֣ל וּלְלֵאָ֑ה הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה אֶל־צֹאנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And sent Jacob and called Rachel and Leah [to] the field, to his flock.
pieces: Jacob therefore called Rachel and Leah out to the pasture where he had his flock.

L.4: And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flock was,

R.4: So Jacob sent a message to Rachel and Leah. He asked them to come out to the field where his flocks were.

decisions.choice: to the field: away from listeners
decisions.reason: Jacob talks with his wives in the open country, away from Laban's household, where no one could overhear.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ן רֹאֶ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י אֲבִיכֶ֔ן כִּֽי־אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אֵלַ֖י כִּתְמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֑ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֔י הָיָ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, seeing [am] I [the] face of your father, that not [is] it toward me as yesterday [and] three days ago; but [the] God of my father has been with me.
pieces: He told them, "I can tell from your father's face that he is not the same toward me as he was. But the God of my father has stood by me.

L.5: and he said to them, "I see your father's face, that it is not toward me as before. But the God of my father has been with me.

R.5: He said to them, "I can see that your father does not like me anymore. But the God of my father has been with me.

decisions.choice: the God of my father: God known through Isaac
decisions.reason: Jacob names God by his relationship with his father's family (verse 42; 28:13), in contrast with Laban's household and its gods (verse 19).

records.source: וְאַתֵּ֖נָה יְדַעְתֶּ֑ן כִּ֚י בְּכָל־כֹּחִ֔י עָבַ֖דְתִּי אֶת־אֲבִיכֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And you, you know that with all my strength I have served your father.
pieces: You yourselves know that I have given your father my full strength in his service.

L.6: And you yourselves know that I have served your father with all my strength.

R.6: You know that I have worked for your father as hard as I could.

records.source: וַאֲבִיכֶן֙ הֵ֣תֶל בִּ֔י וְהֶחֱלִ֥ף אֶת־מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּ֖י עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת מֹנִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־נְתָנ֣וֹ אֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהָרַ֖ע עִמָּדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And your father has cheated me and has changed my wage ten times; but not has permitted him God to do harm with me.
pieces: Even so, your father has tricked me and altered my wages time after time. But God would not let him do me any harm.

L.7: Yet your father has cheated me and changed my wages ten times. But God did not let him harm me.

R.7: But your father has cheated me. He has changed my pay over and over again. But God did not let him hurt me.

decisions.choice: ten times: many times
decisions.reason: "Ten times" is a round number meaning again and again (Numbers 14:22; Job 19:3). The chapter before tells of only one bargain, so Laban had kept changing its terms.

decisions.choice: time after time (B); over and over again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the round number; Literal keeps "ten times" (m1).

records.source: אִם־כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֗ר נְקֻדִּים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׂכָרֶ֔ךָ וְיָלְד֥וּ כָל־הַצֹּ֖אן נְקֻדִּ֑ים וְאִם־כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֗ר עֲקֻדִּים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׂכָרֶ֔ךָ וְיָלְד֥וּ כָל־הַצֹּ֖אן עֲקֻדִּֽים׃
records.gloss: If thus he said, speckled [ones] will be your wage, then bore all the flock speckled [ones]; and if thus he said, striped [ones] will be your wage, then bore all the flock striped [ones].
pieces: Whenever he said, 'The speckled ones will be your pay,' the whole flock had speckled young. And whenever he said, 'The striped ones will be your pay,' the whole flock bore striped young.

L.8: If he said, 'The speckled shall be your wages,' then all the flock bore speckled young; and if he said, 'The striped shall be your wages,' then all the flock bore striped young.

R.8: When he said, 'You can have the speckled animals as your pay,' then all the animals had speckled babies. When he said, 'You can have the striped ones as your pay,' then all the animals had striped babies.

records.source: וַיַּצֵּ֧ל אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־מִקְנֵ֥ה אֲבִיכֶ֖ם וַיִּתֶּן־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And has taken away God [the] livestock of your father and given [it] to me.
pieces: So it is God who has taken your father's livestock away from him and given them to me.

L.9: Thus God has taken away your father's livestock and given it to me.

R.9: This is how God took your father's animals and gave them to me.

decisions.choice: God has taken away: Jacob credits God, not his sticks
decisions.reason: Jacob tells his wives that the increase was God's doing (30:37-43). The verb (natsal) usually means to rescue; God has "rescued" the flocks from Laban, a word Rachel and Leah repeat in verse 16.

decisions.choice: your father: "your" is masculine plural
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has a masculine form of "your" here, where a feminine would be expected for the two wives. Hebrew sometimes uses the masculine for mixed or general address, and the meaning is the same.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֵת֙ יַחֵ֣ם הַצֹּ֔אן וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֛י וָאֵ֖רֶא בַּחֲל֑וֹם וְהִנֵּ֤ה הָֽעַתֻּדִים֙ הָעֹלִ֣ים עַל־הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּבְרֻדִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] time of the mating of the flock, and I lifted my eyes and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats going up on the flock [were] striped, speckled, and mottled.
pieces: At the season when the flocks were mating, I lifted my eyes and saw in a dream that the male goats mounting the females were striped, speckled and mottled.

L.10: And at the time when the flock was mating, I lifted up my eyes and saw in a dream, and look, the male goats that were mounting the flock were striped, speckled and mottled.

R.10: One time when the animals were mating, I had a dream. In my dream I saw that the male goats that were mating with the females had stripes, speckles and spots.

decisions.choice: mottled: marked with patches
decisions.reason: The word (barod) seems to mean spotted with patches like hail (barad). It is used only here and in verse 12 and of horses in Zechariah 6:3, 6.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י מַלְאַ֧ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים בַּחֲל֖וֹם יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said to me [the] angel of God in the dream, Jacob, and I said, here I [am].
pieces: And the angel of God called to me in the dream, 'Jacob!' 'Yes, I am here,' I answered.

L.11: And the angel of God said to me in the dream, 'Jacob,' and I said, 'Here I am.'

R.11: In the dream the angel of God called to me, 'Jacob!' I answered, 'Here I am.'

decisions.choice: the angel of God: God speaking through his messenger
decisions.reason: The angel speaks as God himself in verse 13 ("I am the God of Bethel"), as the angel of the LORD does in 16:10 and 22:11-12.

decisions.choice: Here I am: ready to listen and obey
decisions.reason: The answer (hinneni) is the reply of a servant ready to hear, as Abraham answered God (22:1, 11).

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שָׂא־נָ֨א עֵינֶ֤יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ כָּל־הָֽעַתֻּדִים֙ הָעֹלִ֣ים עַל־הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּבְרֻדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י רָאִ֔יתִי אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָבָ֖ן עֹ֥שֶׂה לָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And he said, lift please your eyes and see: all the male goats going up on the flock [are] striped, speckled, and mottled; for I have seen all that Laban [is] doing to you.
pieces: He said, 'Raise your eyes and look: every male goat mounting the flock is striped, speckled or mottled, for I have taken note of everything Laban is doing to you.

L.12: And he said, 'Lift up your eyes and see: all the male goats mounting the flock are striped, speckled and mottled, for I have seen all that Laban is doing to you.

R.12: He said, 'Look! All the male goats that are mating are striped, speckled or spotted. I am doing this because I have seen all the wrong things Laban is doing to you.

decisions.choice: I have seen all that Laban is doing: God sees the wronged
decisions.reason: As God saw Leah when she was unloved (29:31-32), he sees Jacob cheated, and he acts for him. The words recall God seeing Israel's oppression in Egypt (Exodus 3:7).

decisions.choice: I have seen: the angel speaks as God
decisions.reason: In the dream the angel's "I" is God's own, as verse 13 makes plain.

decisions.choice: I am doing this because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out how the dream and the reason belong together.

records.source: אָנֹכִ֤י הָאֵל֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָשַׁ֤חְתָּ שָּׁם֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָדַ֥רְתָּ לִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם נֶ֑דֶר עַתָּ֗ה ק֥וּם צֵא֙ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְשׁ֖וּב אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ מוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: I [am] the God [of] Bethel, where you anointed there a pillar, where you vowed to me there a vow; now arise, go out from this land and return to [the] land of your kindred.
pieces: I am the God of Bethel, where you poured oil on a pillar and made a vow to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Now get up, leave this land, and go back to the land of your birth.'"

L.13: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar, where you made a vow to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Now arise, go out from this land and return to the land of your kindred.'"

R.13: I am the God you met at Bethel. There you poured oil on a stone pillar and made a promise to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Now get ready and leave this land. Go back to the land where you were born.'"

decisions.choice: the God of Bethel
alternatives: the God who appeared to you at Bethel (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is literally "I am the God Bethel", an unusual phrase that means the God who met Jacob at Bethel. The Septuagint reads "I am the God who appeared to you in the place of God", a smoother text that explains the phrase. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: where you anointed a pillar and made a vow: Jacob's night at Bethel
decisions.reason: Jacob set up the stone he had slept on as a pillar, poured oil on it and vowed that if God brought him home safely, the LORD would be his God (28:18-22). God now calls him to go home and keep the vow.

decisions.choice: me (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The angel speaks as God, so "me" takes the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וַתַּ֤עַן רָחֵל֙ וְלֵאָ֔ה וַתֹּאמַ֖רְנָה ל֑וֹ הַע֥וֹד לָ֛נוּ חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And answered Rachel and Leah and said to him, [is there] still to us a portion and an inheritance in [the] house of our father?
pieces: Rachel and Leah replied, "Is there anything left for us to inherit from our father's house?

L.14: And Rachel and Leah answered and said to him, "Is there still any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house?

R.14: Rachel and Leah answered Jacob, "There is nothing left for us to inherit from our father.

decisions.choice: portion and inheritance: their share in the family property
decisions.reason: Daughters normally received a dowry or a gift from their father rather than an inheritance. The sisters mean that their father has left them nothing at all and that they have no reason to stay.

records.source: הֲל֧וֹא נָכְרִיּ֛וֹת נֶחְשַׁ֥בְנוּ ל֖וֹ כִּ֣י מְכָרָ֑נוּ וַיֹּ֥אכַל גַּם־אָכ֖וֹל אֶת־כַּסְפֵּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: Not [as] foreigners are we regarded by him? For he has sold us and has also surely consumed our money.
pieces: He treats us as outsiders. He sold us, and then he swallowed up the whole price paid for us.

L.15: Are we not counted by him as foreigners? For he has sold us, and he has also used up our money completely.

R.15: He treats us like strangers! He sold us to you, and then he spent all the money he got for us.

decisions.choice: he has sold us and consumed our money: the bride price
decisions.reason: Jacob's fourteen years of work were the bride price for his wives (29:18, 27). Part of a bride price was expected to come back to the bride, perhaps as her dowry. Laban kept all the value of Jacob's work for himself, as if he had sold his daughters to a stranger.

decisions.choice: the whole price paid for us (B); all the money he got for us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "our money" was (m1).

records.source: כִּ֣י כָל־הָעֹ֗שֶׁר אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּ֤יל אֱלֹהִים֙ מֵֽאָבִ֔ינוּ לָ֥נוּ ה֖וּא וּלְבָנֵ֑ינוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֵלֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵֽׂה׃
records.gloss: For all the wealth that has taken away God from our father, to us it [belongs] and to our children; and now, all that has said God to you, do.
pieces: Whatever riches God has taken from our father are ours and our children's by right. Now then, do everything God has said to you."

L.16: For all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children. So now, do all that God has said to you."

R.16: All the riches God took away from our father really belong to us and our children. So go ahead and do everything God told you."

records.source: וַיָּ֖קָם יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיִּשָּׂ֛א אֶת־בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶת־נָשָׁ֖יו עַל־הַגְּמַלִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And arose Jacob and lifted his children and his wives onto the camels.
pieces: Jacob set out at once, putting his children and wives on camels,

L.17: And Jacob arose and set his children and his wives on the camels,

R.17: So Jacob got ready to leave. He put his children and his wives on camels.

records.source: וַיִּנְהַ֣ג אֶת־כָּל־מִקְנֵ֗הוּ וְאֶת־כָּל־רְכֻשׁוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָכָ֔שׁ מִקְנֵה֙ קִנְיָנ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָכַ֖שׁ בְּפַדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם לָב֛וֹא אֶל־יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו אַ֥רְצָה כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And he drove all his livestock and all his property which he had acquired, [the] livestock of his acquiring which he had acquired in Paddan-aram, to go to Isaac his father, to [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: and he drove off all his herds and all the goods he had gained in Paddan-aram, the livestock that he had acquired there, to go to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.

L.18: and he drove away all his livestock and all his property that he had gained, the livestock he had acquired, which he had gained in Paddan-aram, to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.

R.18: He drove all his animals ahead of him. He took everything he had gotten in Paddan-aram. He set off to go back to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.

decisions.choice: Paddan-aram: the region of Haran
decisions.reason: Paddan-aram ("the plain of Aram") is the region of Haran in northern Mesopotamia, where Abraham's relatives lived (25:20; 28:2). Its people were Arameans (verse 20).

records.source: וְלָבָ֣ן הָלַ֔ךְ לִגְזֹ֖ז אֶת־צֹאנ֑וֹ וַתִּגְנֹ֣ב רָחֵ֔ל אֶת־הַתְּרָפִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאָבִֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and stole Rachel the teraphim which [belonged] to her father.
pieces: Laban was away shearing his sheep, and Rachel took the household gods that belonged to her father.

L.19: Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole the household gods that belonged to her father.

R.19: Laban had gone away to cut the wool from his sheep. While he was gone, Rachel stole the small idols of the family gods that belonged to her father.

decisions.choice: household gods: teraphim
decisions.reason: The teraphim were figures of gods kept in a home, small enough to hide in a camel saddle (verse 34); in 1 Samuel 19:13 one is large enough to pass for a man. They may have been thought to protect the household or to give guidance (Ezekiel 21:21). Laban calls them "my gods" (verse 30). The text does not say why Rachel took them.

decisions.choice: shearing time: the master away from home
decisions.reason: Sheepshearing was a busy season and a festival, which kept the owner away from home for days (38:12-13; 1 Samuel 25:4-8). It gave Jacob his chance to leave.

decisions.choice: the small idols of the family gods
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the teraphim were (m1).

records.source: וַיִּגְנֹ֣ב יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶת־לֵ֥ב לָבָ֖ן הָאֲרַמִּ֑י עַל־בְּלִי֙ הִגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י בֹרֵ֖חַ הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And stole Jacob [the] heart of Laban the Aramean, by not telling him that fleeing [was] he.
pieces: And Jacob outwitted Laban the Aramean by not letting him know that he meant to run away.

L.20: And Jacob stole the heart of Laban the Aramean, by not telling him that he was fleeing.

R.20: Jacob tricked Laban the Aramean. He did not tell Laban that he was leaving.

decisions.choice: stole the heart: deceived
decisions.reason: "Steal the heart", that is, the mind, means to deceive (2 Samuel 15:6). The verb is the one used of Rachel in verse 19: she steals the gods, Jacob steals Laban's mind. Laban repeats the charge in verses 26-27.

decisions.choice: Laban the Aramean
decisions.reason: Laban is called an Aramean, as in 25:20. The name points to the line between Jacob's family and the Arameans, which will be marked by a boundary heap in verses 44-53.

decisions.choice: stole the heart (L); outwitted (B); tricked (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom so the wordplay with verse 19 shows; Balanced and Readable give its sense (m1).

records.source: וַיִּבְרַ֥ח הוּא֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר אֶת־הַנָּהָ֑ר וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־פָּנָ֖יו הַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: And fled he and all that [belonged] to him, and he arose and crossed the River, and he set his face [toward the] hill country of Gilead.
pieces: He fled with all that was his. Setting out, he crossed the Euphrates and turned toward the hill country of Gilead.

L.21: So he fled with all that he had, and arose and crossed the River, and set his face toward the hill country of Gilead.

R.21: So Jacob ran away with everything he had. He crossed the Euphrates River and went toward the hill country of Gilead.

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" in the Hebrew Bible usually means the Euphrates (15:18; Joshua 24:2).

decisions.choice: the hill country of Gilead: east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead is the high wooded land east of the Jordan, the edge of the land God promised. From Haran it was several hundred miles away.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the river (m1).

records.source: וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְלָבָ֖ן בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח יַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And it was told to Laban on the third day that had fled Jacob.
pieces: Three days later Laban learned that Jacob had run away.

L.22: And on the third day Laban was told that Jacob had fled.

R.22: On the third day, someone told Laban that Jacob had run away.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־אֶחָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף אַחֲרָ֔יו דֶּ֖רֶךְ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיַּדְבֵּ֥ק אֹת֖וֹ בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: And he took his kinsmen with him and pursued after him a journey of seven days, and overtook him in [the] hill country of Gilead.
pieces: Laban took his relatives with him and went after Jacob, and after seven days' travel he caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.

L.23: And he took his kinsmen with him and pursued him for seven days' journey, and he caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.

R.23: Laban took his relatives with him and chased after Jacob for seven days. He caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.

decisions.choice: kinsmen: literally "brothers"
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means relatives, the men of Laban's clan, an armed band.

decisions.choice: seven days' journey
decisions.reason: Jacob's slow train of flocks and children would have taken much longer to cover the distance; Laban's men, moving fast, caught up in seven days.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־לָבָ֥ן הָאֲרַמִּ֖י בַּחֲלֹ֣ם הַלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הִשָּׁ֧מֶר לְךָ֛ פֶּן־תְּדַבֵּ֥ר עִֽם־יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִטּ֥וֹב עַד־רָֽע׃
records.gloss: And came God to Laban the Aramean in a dream of the night and said to him, take heed to yourself lest you speak with Jacob from good to bad.
pieces: But in a dream by night God came to Laban the Aramean and warned him, "Watch yourself: do not say a word to Jacob, good or bad."

L.24: But God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream by night and said to him, "Be careful not to speak to Jacob either good or bad."

R.24: But that night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream. God said to him, "Be careful! Do not try to make Jacob come back, and do not threaten him."

decisions.choice: either good or bad: anything to change his course
decisions.reason: The phrase "from good to bad" means anything at all (24:50). Laban is not to persuade or force Jacob to return. He does speak to Jacob, but he cannot harm him (verse 29).

decisions.choice: Do not try to make Jacob come back, and do not threaten him
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1).

records.source: וַיַּשֵּׂ֥ג לָבָ֖ן אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיַעֲקֹ֗ב תָּקַ֤ע אֶֽת־אָהֳלוֹ֙ בָּהָ֔ר וְלָבָ֛ן תָּקַ֥ע אֶת־אֶחָ֖יו בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: And overtook Laban Jacob, and Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban pitched with his kinsmen in [the] hill country of Gilead.
pieces: Laban caught up with Jacob, who had pitched his tent in the hills, and Laban and his relatives camped in the hill country of Gilead too.

L.25: And Laban overtook Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban with his kinsmen pitched in the hill country of Gilead.

R.25: Laban caught up with Jacob in the hill country of Gilead. Jacob had set up his tents there, and Laban and his relatives set up their tents there too.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ וַתִּגְנֹ֖ב אֶת־לְבָבִ֑י וַתְּנַהֵג֙ אֶת־בְּנֹתַ֔י כִּשְׁבֻי֖וֹת חָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And said Laban to Jacob, what have you done? And you stole my heart and drove away my daughters like captives of [the] sword.
pieces: "What is this you have done?" Laban said to Jacob. "You have tricked me and driven my daughters off like prisoners taken at sword point.

L.26: And Laban said to Jacob, "What have you done? You have stolen my heart and carried off my daughters like captives of the sword.

R.26: Laban said to Jacob, "What have you done? You tricked me. You took my daughters away like prisoners captured in a war.

decisions.choice: stolen my heart: deceived me
decisions.reason: The idiom of verse 20. Laban, who deceived Jacob on his wedding night (29:25), now complains of being deceived.

records.source: לָ֤מָּה נַחְבֵּ֨אתָ֙ לִבְרֹ֔חַ וַתִּגְנֹ֖ב אֹתִ֑י וְלֹא־הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י וָֽאֲשַׁלֵּחֲךָ֛ בְּשִׂמְחָ֥ה וּבְשִׁרִ֖ים בְּתֹ֥ף וּבְכִנּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Why did you hide yourself to flee and steal me, and not tell me, and I would have sent you away with joy and with songs, with tambourine and with lyre?
pieces: Why did you slip away in secret and fool me, without a word to me? I would have given you a send-off with celebrating and singing, with drums and harps.

L.27: Why did you flee secretly and steal away from me, and not tell me? I would have sent you off with joy and songs, with tambourine and lyre.

R.27: Why did you run away secretly and trick me? Why did you not tell me? I would have given you a happy farewell party, with songs and music on tambourines and harps.

decisions.choice: tambourine and lyre: the music of a farewell
decisions.reason: The tambourine (tof), a hand drum, and the lyre (kinnor), a small stringed instrument, were played at feasts and celebrations (4:21; Exodus 15:20). Laban's claim that he would have sent Jacob off with a party sounds hollow after twenty years of dealings.

records.source: וְלֹ֣א נְטַשְׁתַּ֔נִי לְנַשֵּׁ֥ק לְבָנַ֖י וְלִבְנֹתָ֑י עַתָּ֖ה הִסְכַּ֥לְתָּֽ עֲשֽׂוֹ׃
records.gloss: And not you allowed me to kiss my sons and my daughters; now you have acted foolishly in doing [so].
pieces: You gave me no chance to kiss my grandchildren and daughters farewell. That was a foolish thing to do.

L.28: And you did not let me kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have done a foolish thing.

R.28: You did not let me say goodbye to my grandchildren and my daughters with a kiss. That was foolish of you.

decisions.choice: my sons: my grandchildren
decisions.reason: "Sons" includes descendants; Laban means his daughters' children (verse 43).

decisions.choice: grandchildren
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who Laban's "sons" are (m1).

records.source: יֶשׁ־לְאֵ֣ל יָדִ֔י לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עִמָּכֶ֖ם רָ֑ע וֵֽאלֹהֵ֨י אֲבִיכֶ֜ם אֶ֣מֶשׁ׀אָמַ֧ר אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֗ר הִשָּׁ֧מֶר לְךָ֛ מִדַּבֵּ֥ר עִֽם־יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִטּ֥וֹב עַד־רָֽע׃
records.gloss: There is [it] in [the] power of my hand to do with you harm; but [the] God of your father last night said to me, saying, take heed to yourself from speaking with Jacob from good to bad.
pieces: It is within my power to do you all harm, but last night the God of your father spoke to me: 'Watch yourself: do not say a word to Jacob, good or bad.'

L.29: It is in my power to do you harm. But the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, 'Be careful not to speak to Jacob either good or bad.'

R.29: I have enough power to hurt you. But last night the God of your father spoke to me. He said, 'Be careful! Do not try to make Jacob come back, and do not threaten him.'

decisions.choice: it is in my power: literally "there is to the god of my hand"
decisions.reason: The phrase (yesh le'el yadi) means "I am able" (Deuteronomy 28:32; Micah 2:1). The word el here means power or strength.

decisions.choice: you, your: plural
decisions.reason: Laban speaks to Jacob and all his household: "to do you all harm", "the God of your (family's) father".

decisions.choice: the God of your father: Laban knows whose God protects Jacob
decisions.reason: Laban calls him "the God of your father", not his own god. He admits that this God has stopped him.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ הָלֹ֣ךְ הָלַ֔כְתָּ כִּֽי־נִכְסֹ֥ף נִכְסַ֖פְתָּה לְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ לָ֥מָּה גָנַ֖בְתָּ אֶת־אֱלֹהָֽי׃
records.gloss: And now, surely you have gone, because greatly you longed for [the] house of your father; why did you steal my gods?
pieces: Now I understand you went away because you were homesick for your father's house. But why did you steal my gods?"

L.30: And now you have surely gone because you longed greatly for your father's house. But why did you steal my gods?"

R.30: I know you left because you wanted so much to go back to your father's home. But why did you steal my gods?"

decisions.choice: my gods: the household gods
decisions.reason: Laban calls the teraphim of verse 19 "my gods". The story quietly mocks them: gods that can be stolen, hidden in a saddle and sat on (verse 34). Compare Isaiah 46:1-2.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַן יַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְלָבָ֑ן כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔אתִי כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן־תִּגְזֹ֥ל אֶת־בְּנוֹתֶ֖יךָ מֵעִמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And answered Jacob and said to Laban, because I was afraid, for I said, lest you tear away your daughters from me.
pieces: Jacob replied, "I was afraid. I told myself you would snatch your daughters away from me.

L.31: And Jacob answered and said to Laban, "Because I was afraid, for I thought, 'You might take your daughters from me by force.'

R.31: Jacob said to Laban, "I was afraid you would force your daughters to stay with you. That is why I left in secret.

decisions.choice: I thought: literally "I said"
decisions.reason: As often, "say" means to say to oneself (26:9).

decisions.choice: take by force (gazal): seize, rob
decisions.reason: The verb means to snatch or seize by force, as a robber does (Deuteronomy 28:31).

records.source: עִ֠ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֣א אֶת־אֱלֹהֶיךָ֮ לֹ֣א יִֽחְיֶה֒ נֶ֣גֶד אַחֵ֧ינוּ הַֽכֶּר־לְךָ֛ מָ֥ה עִמָּדִ֖י וְקַֽח־לָ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־יָדַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב כִּ֥י רָחֵ֖ל גְּנָבָֽתַם׃
records.gloss: With whom you will find your gods, he will not live; before our kinsmen examine for yourself what [is] with me, and take [it] for yourself. And not knew Jacob that Rachel had stolen them.
pieces: As for your gods, whoever has them will be put to death. With our relatives as witnesses, search for anything of yours that I have, and take it." Jacob had no idea that Rachel had stolen them.

L.32: Anyone with whom you find your gods shall not live. In the presence of our kinsmen, look for yourself what of yours is with me, and take it." For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.

R.32: If you find your gods with anyone here, that person will die. Our relatives can watch while you look through my things. If you find anything that belongs to you, take it." Jacob had no idea that Rachel was the one who had taken them.

decisions.choice: shall not live: Jacob's rash word
decisions.reason: Jacob unknowingly puts the life of the wife he loves at stake; the reader knows what he does not. Rachel dies soon afterward, on the road to Bethlehem (35:16-19). Compare Joseph's brothers in 44:9.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א לָבָ֜ן בְּאֹ֥הֶל יַעֲקֹ֣ב׀וּבְאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֗ה וּבְאֹ֛הֶל שְׁתֵּ֥י הָאֲמָהֹ֖ת וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑א וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֵאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּאֹ֥הֶל רָחֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And went Laban into [the] tent of Jacob, and into [the] tent of Leah, and into [the] tent of the two slave women, and not he found [them]; and he went out from [the] tent of Leah and went into [the] tent of Rachel.
pieces: Laban searched Jacob's tent, Leah's tent and the tent of the two female servants, and found nothing. Coming out of Leah's tent, he went on into Rachel's.

L.33: So Laban went into Jacob's tent and into Leah's tent and into the tent of the two slave women, but he did not find them. And he went out of Leah's tent and entered Rachel's tent.

R.33: So Laban searched Jacob's tent. Then he searched Leah's tent and the tent of the two female servants, but he did not find his gods. He left Leah's tent and went into Rachel's tent.

decisions.choice: slave women: Bilhah and Zilpah
decisions.reason: The word (amah) is the one used of Bilhah in 30:3. Each wife had her own tent, as was the custom in a large household (24:67).

decisions.choice: female servants
decisions.reason: "Female servants" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m1) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וְרָחֵ֞ל לָקְחָ֣ה אֶת־הַתְּרָפִ֗ים וַתְּשִׂמֵ֛ם בְּכַ֥ר הַגָּמָ֖ל וַתֵּ֣שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיְמַשֵּׁ֥שׁ לָבָ֛ן אֶת־כָּל־הָאֹ֖הֶל וְלֹ֥א מָצָֽא׃
records.gloss: And Rachel had taken the teraphim and put them in [the] saddle of the camel and sat on them; and felt Laban all the tent and not found [them].
pieces: Rachel, though, had taken the household gods, tucked them into her camel saddle and sat down on top of them. Laban felt through the whole tent without finding them.

L.34: Now Rachel had taken the household gods and put them in the camel's saddle and sat on them. And Laban felt all through the tent, but did not find them.

R.34: But Rachel had taken the idols and put them inside the saddle of her camel. She was sitting on them. Laban looked everywhere in the tent, but he did not find them.

decisions.choice: the camel's saddle: a woman's riding seat
decisions.reason: The word (kar) is a cushioned saddle or basket seat used by a woman riding a camel; things could be hidden inside it.

decisions.choice: felt all through: groped
decisions.reason: The verb (mishesh) means to feel about with the hands, as blind Isaac felt Jacob (27:12, 22). Laban searches by touch, but cannot find what Rachel sits on.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־אָבִ֗יהָ אַל־יִ֨חַר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֣י ל֤וֹא אוּכַל֙ לָק֣וּם מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ כִּי־דֶ֥רֶךְ נָשִׁ֖ים לִ֑י וַיְחַפֵּ֕שׂ וְלֹ֥א מָצָ֖א אֶת־הַתְּרָפִֽים׃
records.gloss: And she said to her father, let not burn in [the] eyes of my lord that not I am able to rise before you, for [the] way of women [is] to me; and he searched and not found the teraphim.
pieces: She said to her father, "Please, my lord, do not be offended that I do not rise before you; it is my time of the month." He went on searching, but the household gods were not to be found.

L.35: And she said to her father, "Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise before you, for the way of women is upon me." So he searched but did not find the household gods.

R.35: Rachel said to her father, "Sir, please do not be angry with me for not standing up. I am having my monthly period." Laban kept looking, but he did not find the idols.

decisions.choice: the way of women: a woman's monthly period
decisions.reason: The phrase means menstruation (compare 18:11). Rising before a father or elder was a mark of respect (Leviticus 19:32).

decisions.choice: my lord: a respectful address
decisions.reason: Rachel addresses her father with the respect a daughter owed. The scene has a sharp irony: the later Law counted whatever a woman sat on during her period as unclean (Leviticus 15:20), and here Laban's gods are under her.

decisions.choice: let it not burn in the eyes of my lord: do not be angry
decisions.reason: "Let it not burn" means let it not anger (45:5).

records.source: וַיִּ֥חַר לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיָּ֣רֶב בְּלָבָ֑ן וַיַּ֤עַן יַעֲקֹב֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְלָבָ֔ן מַה־פִּשְׁעִי֙ מַ֣ה חַטָּאתִ֔י כִּ֥י דָלַ֖קְתָּ אַחֲרָֽי׃
records.gloss: And it burned to Jacob, and he quarreled with Laban; and answered Jacob and said to Laban, what [is] my offense, what [is] my sin, that you have hotly pursued after me?
pieces: Jacob became angry and argued with Laban. "What wrong have I done?" he said to him. "What is my offense, that you came after me in such hot pursuit?

L.36: And Jacob became angry and quarreled with Laban. And Jacob answered and said to Laban, "What is my offense? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me?

R.36: Then Jacob became angry with Laban. He said, "What have I done wrong? What law have I broken that you chased after me like this?

decisions.choice: quarreled (riv): brought a complaint
decisions.reason: The verb is used of legal disputes; Jacob speaks like a man bringing his case before witnesses (verse 37).

decisions.choice: offense and sin
decisions.reason: The two words (pesha, chatta't) are the main words for wrongdoing: breaking faith and missing the mark. Jacob challenges Laban to name any wrong he has done.

decisions.choice: hotly pursued: chased in hot pursuit
decisions.reason: The verb (dalaq) means to burn, and so to chase hotly (1 Samuel 17:53).

records.source: כִּֽי־מִשַּׁ֣שְׁתָּ אֶת־כָּל־כֵּלַ֗י מַה־מָּצָ֨אתָ֙ מִכֹּ֣ל כְּלֵי־בֵיתֶ֔ךָ שִׂ֣ים כֹּ֔ה נֶ֥גֶד אַחַ֖י וְאַחֶ֑יךָ וְיוֹכִ֖יחוּ בֵּ֥ין שְׁנֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: For you have felt through all my things; what have you found of all [the] things of your house? Put [it] here before my kinsmen and your kinsmen, and let them decide between [the] two of us.
pieces: You have gone through every one of my things. Have you found a single thing from your house? Lay it out here before your kinsmen and mine, and they can settle the matter between us.

L.37: You have felt through all my goods. What have you found of all your household goods? Set it here before my kinsmen and your kinsmen, and let them judge between the two of us.

R.37: You have searched through everything I own. Did you find anything that belongs to you? Put it here in front of your relatives and mine. Let them decide which of us is right.

decisions.choice: let them judge between us: kinsmen as a court
decisions.reason: Disputes in a clan were settled by the elders and family as witnesses and judges (Ruth 4:9-11). Jacob asks for a public verdict.

records.source: זֶה֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים שָׁנָ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ רְחֵלֶ֥יךָ וְעִזֶּ֖יךָ לֹ֣א שִׁכֵּ֑לוּ וְאֵילֵ֥י צֹאנְךָ֖ לֹ֥א אָכָֽלְתִּי׃
records.gloss: This twenty years I [have been] with you; your ewes and your female goats have not miscarried, and [the] rams of your flock not I have eaten.
pieces: For twenty years I was with you. Not one of your ewes or she-goats miscarried, and I never ate a ram of your flock.

L.38: These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not miscarried, and I have not eaten the rams of your flock.

R.38: I have worked for you for twenty years. All that time, your sheep and goats did not lose their young. I never ate any of your rams.

decisions.choice: miscarried: lost their young
decisions.reason: The verb (shakal) means to be bereaved, here of animals losing their young before birth. Jacob claims that his care kept the flocks healthy.

records.source: טְרֵפָה֙ לֹא־הֵבֵ֣אתִי אֵלֶ֔יךָ אָנֹכִ֣י אֲחַטֶּ֔נָּה מִיָּדִ֖י תְּבַקְשֶׁ֑נָּה גְּנֻֽבְתִ֣י י֔וֹם וּגְנֻֽבְתִ֖י לָֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: A torn [animal] not I brought to you; I, I bore its loss; from my hand you required it, stolen by day and stolen by night.
pieces: When a wild animal killed one, I did not bring it to you to show it was not my fault; I made up the loss myself. You made me pay for anything stolen, by day or by night.

L.39: That which was torn by beasts I did not bring to you; I bore the loss of it myself. You required it of my hand, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.

R.39: If wild animals killed one of your animals, I did not bring it to you to prove it was not my fault. I paid for it myself. You made me pay for any animal that was stolen, whether in the day or at night.

decisions.choice: torn by beasts: the shepherd's custom
decisions.reason: A hired shepherd could bring the remains of an animal killed by a wild beast as proof, and so not have to pay for it (Exodus 22:13; Amos 3:12). Jacob bore those losses himself, more than custom required.

decisions.choice: to show it was not my fault (B); to prove it was not my fault (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why a shepherd would bring a torn animal (m1).

records.source: הָיִ֧יתִי בַיּ֛וֹם אֲכָלַ֥נִי חֹ֖רֶב וְקֶ֣רַח בַּלָּ֑יְלָה וַתִּדַּ֥ד שְׁנָתִ֖י מֵֽעֵינָֽי׃
records.gloss: I was [thus]: in the day consumed me heat, and frost in the night, and fled my sleep from my eyes.
pieces: That is how it was: by day the heat wore me down, by night the cold, and I could not sleep.

L.40: This was my lot: by day the heat consumed me, and the cold by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes.

R.40: In the daytime the heat burned me, and at night I was freezing. Many nights I could not sleep.

decisions.choice: the cold: frost
decisions.reason: The word (qerach) is frost or ice. Nights in the hills and the steppe were bitterly cold, even after hot days.

records.gloss: This [has been] to me twenty years in your house; I served you fourteen years for [the] two of your daughters and six years for your flock, and you changed my wage ten times.
pieces: That was my life for twenty years in your house: fourteen years of work for your two daughters and six for your flocks, while you changed my wages again and again.

L.41: These twenty years I have been in your house: I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times.

R.41: For twenty years I was part of your household. I worked fourteen years to earn your two daughters. Then I worked six more years to earn some of your animals. And you changed my pay over and over again.

decisions.choice: fourteen years and six: twenty years of service
decisions.reason: Seven years each for Leah and Rachel (29:20, 27-30), then six years for the flocks (30:25-43).

decisions.choice: again and again (B); over and over again (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, "ten times" means many times.

records.gloss: If not [the] God of my father, [the] God of Abraham and [the] Fear of Isaac, had been for me, surely now empty you would have sent me away. My affliction and [the] toil of my hands has seen God, and he rebuked [you] last night.
pieces: Had the God of my father, the God of Abraham, the One whom Isaac fears, not stood by me, you would have sent me off with empty hands by now. But God saw how I suffered and how hard I toiled, and last night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} verdict."

L.42: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been on my side, surely now you would have sent me away empty-handed. God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave judgment last night."

R.42: The God of my father, the God of Abraham and the God Isaac worships with fear, was with me. If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not been, you would have sent me away with nothing. But God saw my troubles and how hard I worked. So last night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you that you were wrong."

decisions.choice: the Fear of Isaac: a name for God
decisions.reason: The phrase (pachad yitschaq) occurs only here and in verse 53. It most likely means the God whom Isaac feared, that is, revered, or the God who caused terror for Isaac's sake. Some connect pachad with a word meaning "kinsman".

decisions.choice: he gave judgment: he rebuked you
decisions.reason: The verb (yakhach) means to decide a case, and so to rebuke the one in the wrong. Jacob takes Laban's dream (verse 29) as God's verdict in his favor; it is the verb of verse 37, "let them decide".

decisions.choice: he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: "He" and "his" refer to God and take the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: the God Isaac worships with fear
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

records.gloss: And answered Laban and said to Jacob, the daughters [are] my daughters, and the children [are] my children, and the flock [is] my flock, and all that you see, to me it [belongs]; and to my daughters, what can I do to these today, or to their children whom they have borne?
pieces: Laban answered, "These daughters are mine, these children are mine, these flocks are mine; everything in front of you belongs to me. Yet what can I do today for my own daughters, or for the children they have had?

L.43: And Laban answered and said to Jacob, "The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine. But what can I do this day for these my daughters, or for their children whom they have borne?

R.43: Laban answered Jacob, "These women are my daughters. These children are my grandchildren. These flocks are mine. Everything you see belongs to me. But I cannot do anything now to keep my daughters or the children they have had.

decisions.choice: my daughters, my children, my flocks: a father's claim
decisions.reason: In Laban's eyes the household still belongs to its head. He does not concede that Jacob has a right to them, only that he can do nothing to keep them (verse 29).

decisions.choice: what can I do for these?: or "against these"
alternatives: what can I do to these my daughters
decisions.reason: The words can mean "what harm could I do to my own daughters?" or "what can I do for them now?". Either way, Laban gives up his claim and turns to making a treaty.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה לְכָ֛ה נִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית אֲנִ֣י וָאָ֑תָּה וְהָיָ֥ה לְעֵ֖ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And now, come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and let it be for a witness between me and between you.
pieces: So come, you and I will make a covenant, and it will stand as a witness between the two of us."

L.44: So now come, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it be a witness between me and you."

R.44: So come, let us make an agreement, you and I. It will be a sign of the promises we make to each other."

decisions.choice: make a covenant: literally "cut a covenant"
decisions.reason: A covenant (berit) was a binding agreement made with an oath, often with a sacrifice and a shared meal (verses 53-54; 15:9-18; 26:28-30).

decisions.choice: agreement
decisions.reason: Readable says "agreement" for this treaty between two men; elsewhere "covenant" is kept for God's covenants.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֥ח יַעֲקֹ֖ב אָ֑בֶן וַיְרִימֶ֖הָ מַצֵּבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And took Jacob a stone and set it up [as] a pillar.
pieces: Jacob then took a stone and stood it upright as a pillar.

L.45: And Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.

R.45: So Jacob took a large stone and stood it up on its end as a marker.

decisions.choice: a stone set up as a pillar: as at Bethel
decisions.reason: Jacob did the same at Bethel (28:18). A standing stone (matsevah) marked a sacred place or witnessed an agreement (Joshua 24:26-27).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֤ב לְאֶחָיו֙ לִקְט֣וּ אֲבָנִ֔ים וַיִּקְח֥וּ אֲבָנִ֖ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־גָ֑ל וַיֹּ֥אכְלוּ שָׁ֖ם עַל־הַגָּֽל׃
records.gloss: And said Jacob to his kinsmen, gather stones; and they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there by the heap.
pieces: He told his kinsmen to gather stones, and they brought stones and made a heap, and there beside the heap they shared a meal.

L.46: And Jacob said to his kinsmen, "Gather stones." And they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there by the heap.

R.46: Jacob told his relatives, "Gather some stones." So they made a pile of stones. Then they ate a meal there beside the pile.

decisions.choice: they ate there: a covenant meal
decisions.reason: Eating together sealed an agreement (26:30; Exodus 24:11). The meal is told here and again after the oath (verse 54).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָא־ל֣וֹ לָבָ֔ן יְגַ֖ר שָׂהֲדוּתָ֑א וְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב קָ֥רָא ל֖וֹ גַּלְעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And called it Laban Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.
pieces: Laban named it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob named it Galeed.

L.47: And Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, but Jacob called it Galeed.

R.47: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha. Jacob called it Galeed. Both names mean "pile of stones that is a witness."

decisions.choice: Jegar-sahadutha and Galeed: "heap of witness" in two languages
decisions.reason: Laban gives the place an Aramaic name and Jacob a Hebrew one; both mean "heap of witness". These two Aramaic words are the first Aramaic in the Bible. Galeed (gal'ed) also sounds like Gilead, the name of the region (verse 21).

decisions.choice: Both names mean "pile of stones that is a witness"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the names (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֔ן הַגַּ֨ל הַזֶּ֥ה עֵ֛ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינְךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם עַל־כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־שְׁמ֖וֹגַּלְעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And said Laban, the heap this [is] a witness between me and between you today; therefore he called its name Galeed,
pieces: "This heap stands as a witness between you and me today," Laban said. So it was named Galeed,

L.48: And Laban said, "This heap is a witness between me and you today." Therefore its name was called Galeed,

R.48: Laban said, "This pile of stones will remind us of our agreement." That is why it was named Galeed.

decisions.choice: its name was called: or "he called its name"
decisions.reason: The verb is "he called"; it may refer to Jacob (verse 47) or simply mean "it was called".

decisions.choice: will remind us of our agreement
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a witness heap did.

records.source: וְהַמִּצְפָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔ר יִ֥צֶף יְהוָ֖ה בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ כִּ֥י נִסָּתֵ֖ר אִ֥ישׁ מֵרֵעֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: and Mizpah, because he said, may watch YHWH between me and between you, when we are hidden each from his neighbor.
pieces: and also Mizpah, for he said, "Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be on watch between us when we are out of sight of each other.

L.49: and Mizpah, for he said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} watch between me and you when we are out of each other's sight.

R.49: It was also named Mizpah, which means "watchtower," because Laban said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} watch over both of us while we are apart.

decisions.choice: Mizpah: "watchtower", a pun on yitsef, "may he watch"
decisions.reason: The place name and Laban's verb come from the root tsafah, "keep watch". There were several towns called Mizpah; this one, in Gilead, appears again in Judges 10:17 and 11:11.

decisions.choice: May the LORD watch between me and you: a warning, not a blessing
decisions.reason: Laban's words are a call on God to watch over the agreement and punish whichever man breaks it once they can no longer see each other (verse 50).

decisions.choice: the LORD in Laban's mouth
decisions.reason: Laban uses the divine name, as he did in 24:31, 50 and 30:27, though he also keeps household gods (verse 30) and swears by "the God of Nahor" (verse 53).

decisions.choice: which means "watchtower"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

records.source: אִם־תְּעַנֶּ֣ה אֶת־בְּנֹתַ֗י וְאִם־תִּקַּ֤ח נָשִׁים֙ עַל־בְּנֹתַ֔י אֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ עִמָּ֑נוּ רְאֵ֕ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים עֵ֖ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: If you mistreat my daughters, and if you take wives besides my daughters, [though] no one [is] with us, see, God [is] witness between me and between you.
pieces: Should you ever mistreat my daughters or marry other women besides them, though no one else is with us, see, God is witness between you and me."

L.50: If you mistreat my daughters, or if you take wives besides my daughters, though no one is with us, see, God is witness between me and you."

R.50: Do not be cruel to my daughters. Do not marry any other women. Even if no one else sees what you do, remember that God sees, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will judge between us."

decisions.choice: mistreat: oppress, humiliate
decisions.reason: The verb (innah) means to treat harshly or humiliate, as Sarai did Hagar (16:6). Laban, who himself gave Jacob a wife he did not want, now poses as his daughters' protector.

decisions.choice: and he will judge between us
alternatives: is witness between me and you
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for God to be witness: he will hold each to account.

decisions.choice: he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: In Readable, "he" refers to God.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב הִנֵּ֣ה׀הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֗ה וְהִנֵּה֙ הַמַצֵּבָ֔האֲשֶׁ֥ר יָרִ֖יתִי בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Laban to Jacob, here [is] this heap, and here [is] the pillar which I have set up between me and between you.
pieces: Then Laban said to Jacob, "Look at this heap, and look at the pillar I have raised between us.

L.51: And Laban said to Jacob, "See this heap, and see the pillar, which I have set up between me and you.

R.51: Then Laban said to Jacob, "Here is the pile of stones, and here is the stone marker that I have set up between us.

decisions.choice: which I have set up: Laban claims the work
decisions.reason: Jacob set up the pillar and his men made the heap (verses 45-46), but Laban speaks as if he had done it. As the head of the clan he presents himself as the one who makes the treaty.

records.source: עֵ֚ד הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה וְעֵדָ֖ה הַמַּצֵּבָ֑ה אִם־אָ֗נִי לֹֽא־אֶֽעֱבֹ֤ר אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶת־הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה וְאִם־אַ֠תָּה לֹא־תַעֲבֹ֨ר אֵלַ֜י אֶת־הַגַּ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה וְאֶת־הַמַּצֵּבָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לְרָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: Witness [is] this heap, and witness [is] the pillar, that I will not pass beyond this heap to you, and that you will not pass beyond this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.
pieces: The heap and the pillar both bear witness: I will not cross over past this heap to attack you, and you will not cross past this heap and this pillar to attack me.

L.52: This heap is a witness, and the pillar is a witness, that I will not pass beyond this heap to you, and you will not pass beyond this heap and this pillar to me, to do harm.

R.52: This pile of stones and this stone marker remind us of our promise. I will not go past them to hurt you, and you will not go past them to hurt me.

decisions.choice: a boundary: Israel and Aram
decisions.reason: The heap marks a border neither side will cross to make war. In later times Gilead was indeed a borderland between Israel and the Arameans of Damascus (1 Kings 22:3).

records.source: אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י נָחוֹר֙ יִשְׁפְּט֣וּ בֵינֵ֔ינוּ אֱלֹהֵ֖י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּפַ֖חַד אָבִ֥יו יִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: [The] God of Abraham and [the] God of Nahor judge between us, [the] God of their father. And swore Jacob by [the] Fear of his father Isaac.
pieces: Let the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us." So Jacob swore by the One his father Isaac feared.

L.53: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us." And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

R.53: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father Terah, decide who is right if either of us breaks this agreement." So Jacob made a promise in the name of the God his father Isaac worshiped with fear.

decisions.choice: judge: the verb is plural
alternatives: may the gods of Abraham and of Nahor judge between us
decisions.reason: The verb (yishpetu) is plural, so Laban may be thinking of two gods, his family's and Jacob's. The Septuagint has a singular verb. Jacob for his part swears only by the God of Isaac.

decisions.choice: the God of their father
decisions.reason: These words are not in the Septuagint. They link the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor to their father Terah, who served other gods (Joshua 24:2). The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: the Fear of Isaac
decisions.reason: The name of God used in verse 42.

decisions.choice: Terah
decisions.reason: Readable names Abraham and Nahor's father (11:26).

decisions.choice: the God his father Isaac worshiped with fear
decisions.reason: As in verse 42, Readable explains the name.

records.source: וַיִּזְבַּ֨ח יַעֲקֹ֥ב זֶ֨בַח֙ בָּהָ֔ר וַיִּקְרָ֥א לְאֶחָ֖יו לֶאֱכָל־לָ֑חֶם וַיֹּ֣אכְלוּ לֶ֔חֶם וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ בָּהָֽר׃
records.gloss: And sacrificed Jacob a sacrifice on the mountain, and called his kinsmen to eat bread; and they ate bread and spent the night on the mountain.
pieces: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice there on the mountain and invited his relatives to share the meal. They ate together and spent the night on the mountain.

L.54: And Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and called his kinsmen to eat bread. And they ate bread and spent the night on the mountain.

R.54: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain. He invited his relatives to eat a meal together. After they ate, they stayed on the mountain for the night.

decisions.choice: a sacrifice and a meal: sealing the covenant
decisions.reason: This sacrifice (zevach) was one whose meat was eaten by those who offered it. Sharing it bound the two parties together in peace.

decisions.choice: bread: food, a meal
decisions.reason: "Eat bread" means to have a meal (37:25; 43:25).

decisions.choice: share the meal (B); eat a meal (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "bread" here (m2).
